mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, controlling for lagged inflation and GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims exceeding 10,000 while payroll growth remains positive signals a labor market softening without recession, which precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 100000 and GDPC1 > 0 in the same month
regime_hint: Pre-recession softening without jobless claims exceeding 150,000
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive triggered months, SPX 20-day returns are not negative when both PAYEMS > 100000 and GDPC1 > 0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in home building permits (HOUST) for three consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects anticipated economic weakness and equity risk-off flows.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Early warning of a housing contraction cycle
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive when HOUST shows three consecutive monthly declines and other demand proxies (GDPC1, RSAFS) are stable.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 with no offsetting rise in retail sales (CPIAUCSL) indicates supply-side weakness that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 105 and CPIAUCSL does not exceed INDPRO in the same month
regime_hint: Discrepancy between manufacturing and retail activity
failure_condition: In 20 triggered months, SPX 20-day returns are not positive when INDPRO < 105 and CPIAUCSL > INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 2-month decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reduces growth expectations and supports equity valuation expansion.
regime_hint: Deflationary momentum in the consumer price index
failure_condition: Across 12 such windows, 60-day forward returns are not positive when CPIAUCSL remains below 2.0% without a subsequent rebound.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5.5% in a month coinciding with a decline in manufacturing payrolls (GDPC1) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as risk aversion increases.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.5 and GDPC1 < previous month in the same period
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market dislocation in manufacturing
failure_condition: In 30 such triggered windows, SPX 20-day returns are not negative when both UNRATE > 5.5% and GDPC1 declines month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-month surge in retail activity (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 while manufacturing employment (GDPC1) remains flat signals demand expansion without supply catch-up, leading to a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 150000 and GDPC1 is unchanged in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, 5-day forward returns are not negative when PAYEMS > 150000 and GDPC1 is flat.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in retail sales (CPIAUCSL) below trend is a regime-conditional supply shock that predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return in non-recessionary macro regimes (UNRATE < 5%), as it signals consumer weakness and equity reallocation.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and CPIAUCSL < trend for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Non-recessionary environment with persistent retail weakness
failure_condition: In 20 such windows under the specified regime, 20-day forward returns are not positive when CPIAUCSL lags trend and UNRATE remains below 5%.
